title: Ball goes wide: take the half-space
titleKid: Ball wide? Find the in-between strip
brief: Your #6 plays the ball out to your full-back, who has space to run up the touchline.
briefKid: Your midfielder passes wide to your defender, who has space.
question: The ball is out wide on your side. Where do you go?
questionKid: The ball is out wide near you. Where do you go?

takeaway.standard: With the ball wide, get into the ball-side half-space between their midfield and back line: their full-back and centre-back must decide who takes you, and either choice opens a pass.
takeaway.kid: Ball out wide? Find the gap between the wing and the middle.

misconceptions.text: You stayed in the middle next to your #6, so their midfield can cover you both and the full-back has no pass inside.
misconceptions.textKid: You stayed in the middle. Move toward the ball, behind their midfielders.

misconceptions.text: You dropped behind the ball on the same flank, which is a safe pass but beats nobody; get ahead of their midfield in the half-space.
misconceptions.textKid: You went behind the ball. Get ahead, behind their midfielders.

notes: Engine answer since 2026-10-03 (it was authored: layer A dragged the ball-side #8 into the wing lane behind the ball, base (54.5, 56.2), a support spot, not P1). scene.js now sends the ball-side #8 into the half-space between their lines when his full-back has the ball out wide from the middle third (shareFlanks, P1), and the half-space rule judges the channel: base (66.6, 50.2), the best spot (67.6, 53.2) scores 96, 1.2 m from the keyed ideal; the start scores 20. The tighter tolerance (4 x 3 m) is kept. Its third idea is B3 (it was B5, which stood in while P1 had no rule): the answer is praised for the open passing lane it gives the full-back, and with B5 the smaller games praised the spacing across the lanes instead, so no smaller game held. The #9 is keyed on their centre-back's shoulder in the centre lane, as in the P1 picture (he pins the centre-back so the half-space stays free).
